strategy.name: sma200_asymmetric_threshold
strategy.description: After a 200-session SMA warmup, enter only when the close crosses from at-or-below the upper SMA buffer to above it; exit whenever the close is below the lower SMA buffer. Signals are confirmed after the regular-session close and filled at the next regular-session open.
strategy.buy_rule: flat and previous_close <= previous_sma200 * (1 + b_pct / 100) and close > sma200 * (1 + b_pct / 100)
strategy.signal_time: regular-session close after the bar is complete
strategy.positioning: long-only, all cash or all invested, fractional shares

benchmark: buy and hold from first executable open after SMA200 warmup

reporting.reuse_review: promoted from v1 after user review; v2 adds explicit market-overlay checkboxes and a dedicated same-scale CAGR parameter heatmap while preserving the accepted zoom, rebase, and DCA controls
reporting.scenario_layer: browser-only; does not mutate formal backtest artifacts
reporting.left_edge_alignment: scale displayed equity series to the Buy & Hold value on the first common trading day in the visible range; recompute displayed drawdown from that date
reporting.dca: use the visible-range starting Buy & Hold equity as total budget; invest it in N equal tranches at evenly spaced trading sessions; uninvested cash earns zero; each purchase costs 5 bps

research.hypothesis: Across the expanded -3% to 5% SMA200 entry and exit buffers, performance contains broad, economically interpretable plateaus rather than isolated full-sample optimum points; the wider range should reveal whether previously observed boundaries were truncated.
research.primary_metric: 5 bps CAGR, interpreted together with maximum drawdown, Sharpe ratio, turnover, exposure, and plateau geometry
research.selection_rule: Within the largest top-decile CAGR plateau, maximize the 3x3 neighborhood median minus 0.5 times its standard deviation; do not select an isolated global maximum.
research.validation_plan: Freeze candidate regions and selection logic before a separate walk-forward experiment; use only its stitched out-of-sample equity for promotion decisions.
research.promotion_criteria: Independent-ledger reconciliation and all engineering gates pass; the plateau is not an isolated spike; walk-forward results remain useful after costs without parameter selection on the locked test segment.
research.rejection_conditions: Reject or redesign if accounting diverges, performance depends on an isolated or boundary-truncated optimum, cost sensitivity is unstable, or predeclared out-of-sample evidence is materially adverse.
